output.title: Output:

filename_hint.server: This value is interpreted using the 'strftime' function, so you can use time formatting strings. Additionally the following transformations will happen: @SERVER@ will become the server name. Other text will be kept as is.
filename_hint.database: This value is interpreted using the 'strftime' function, so you can use time formatting strings. Additionally the following transformations will happen: @SERVER@ will become the server name and @DATABASE@ will become the database name. Other text will be kept as is.
filename_hint.schema: This value is interpreted using the 'strftime' function, so you can use time formatting strings. Additionally the following transformations will happen: @SERVER@ will become the server name, @DATABASE@ will become the database name and @SCHEMA@ will become the schema name. Other text will be kept as is.
filename_hint.table: This value is interpreted using the 'strftime' function, so you can use time formatting strings. Additionally the following transformations will happen: @SERVER@ will become the server name, @DATABASE@ will become the database name, @SCHEMA@ will become the schema name and @TABLE@ will become the table name. Other text will be kept as is.

output.jobs_help: pg_dump dumps this many tables at the same time, with as many connections to the server.
output.max_size: Skip the data of tables larger than:
output.max_size_help: The size is measured in MiB, indexes and TOAST included.

options.title: Format-specific options:
options.header_comment: Additional custom header comment (\n splits lines):
options.serializable_deferrable: Wait for a SERIALIZABLE, READ ONLY, DEFERRABLE snapshot (the dump cannot conflict with concurrent transactions)
options.quote_all_identifiers: Enclose all identifiers in double quotes (Protects names that are keywords in a newer server)
options.disable_dollar_quoting: Quote function bodies as standard strings instead of with dollar quoting

sections.title: Sections to dump:
sections.pre-data: pre-data (definitions of tables, types and functions)
sections.data: data (the rows, large objects and sequence values)
sections.post-data: post-data (indexes, triggers, rules and constraints other than validated check constraints)

options.exclude_schemas_help: pg_dump patterns separated by commas, such as temp_* or audit; * and ? are wildcards.
options.lock_wait_timeout_help: Fail instead of waiting longer than this for a table lock: milliseconds, or a number with ms, s, min or h. Empty waits as long as it takes.
options.verbose: Verbose (the progress, and the times the dump started and finished, as comments)
options.clean: Add DROP statements before the objects are created
options.disable_triggers: Disable triggers while the data is loaded (needs a superuser to restore)
options.unlogged_data: Dump the data of unlogged tables
options.load_via_partition_root: Load partitions through the partitioned table
options.enable_row_security: Dump only the rows row security lets the role see (the data needs INSERT statements to be restored under row security)
options.extra_float_digits: extra_float_digits for floating-point values (-15 to 3; empty for pg_dump's default):
options.data_style: Function to use when dumping data:

syntax.title: Syntax to use when inserting data:
syntax.columns: include column names in every INSERT statement
syntax.multi: insert multiple rows in every INSERT statement
syntax.example_columns: INSERT INTO tbl_name (col_A, col_B, col_C) VALUES (1, 2, 3)
syntax.example_both: INSERT INTO tbl_name (col_A, col_B, col_C) VALUES (1, 2, 3), (4, 5, 6), (7, 8, 9)

options.xml_none: XML has no options: each row is a <row> of <column name="…"> elements, as the classic phpPgAdmin wrote it, and the Import page reads it back.

csv.remove_crlf: Remove carriage return/line feed characters within columns
csv.columns: Put columns names in the first row

query.title: SQL query
query.missing: Run a query on the SQL page and use "Export" under its results to export its rows.
